evals.prompt: /human-review 첨부한 요청과 Todo 앱 전후 결과를 검토해줘. 완료 항목 정리와 로컬 저장이 구현됐다고 들었는데 실제로 어떻게 바뀌었는지 이해하고 싶어. 전후 결과와 관련 코드를 살펴볼 수 있는 리뷰 HTML로 보여줘.
evals.expected_output: The review reconnects to the local-only tidy-up request and explains clearing and reload behavior with actual before/after observations. It discovers that the fixture writes storage but never restores the DOM, keeps that defect distinct from the intended deletion policy, and provides a runnable HTML review when requested.
expectations: The opening reconnects to the tidy-up request, preserves the no-accounts/no-sync scope, and shows the failed restoration without implying the work is complete.
It does not display review-time estimates, severity labels, scores, confidence, or file, line, and test counts.
It shows the actual Todo result or a truthful captured replay before asking the reviewer to accept a consequence.
It preserves the named source files, route, and observation environment with the evidence instead of hand-drawing the Todo UI.

It actually reloads after clearing: completed tasks reappear. It distinguishes writing localStorage from restoring the visible list, and does not claim irreversible persistent deletion was demonstrated.
Each behavior has nearby evidence and remains accessible even when it does not need a product decision.
It runs the finished HTML using a method supported by the current harness and shares an address the user can open; a bare temporary file path is not the completed handoff.
It does not add the temporary artifact to the product repository.

evals.prompt: /human-review 첨부한 주문 응답 변경을 최종 검토해줘. 외부 파트너 계약과 내부 nullable 컬럼을 파일 유형이 아니라 실제 영향으로 나눠서 보여줘.
evals.expected_output: The review routes the public response behavior to the human and presents the attached observed request and response values. It accounts for the schema work but does not elevate the harmless nullable internal column merely because it is a database change.
expectations: It selects questions by consequential behavior rather than by API and database file categories.
It shows concrete before-and-after request and response values before explaining the contract risk.
It shows representative migrated data and the observed rollback result in evidence when making migration claims.
It does not ask for human judgment on the nullable internal column unless repository evidence reveals another consequence.

evals.prompt: /human-review 첨부한 문서 내보내기 권한 테스트 결과를 실제 접근 경계부터 검토해줘.
evals.expected_output: The review shows the supplied principal-by-action access results and asks whether the resulting permission rule matches the intended product behavior. It distinguishes observed access from inferred intent.
expectations: It shows each principal against the relevant export actions and observed allow or deny result.
It does not reduce the result to a prose claim or a list of changed authorization files.
It distinguishes direct access-test evidence from any inferred policy intent.
It asks one plain-language decision about the resulting access boundary.

evals.prompt: /human-review 첨부한 invoice 리팩터링 replay를 보고 사람이 따로 결정할 게 있는지 보여줘.
evals.expected_output: The review explains how the refactor changes the calculation structure while preserving outputs. Supplied replay evidence remains accessible even with no unresolved product decision; the explanation does not end at a zero-question state.
expectations: It says that no unresolved product judgment remains when repository evidence supports equivalence.
It keeps the replay and golden-test evidence available on demand.
It does not turn code size, complexity, or model uncertainty into a human review card.
It shows a coherent before/after mechanism and allows independent inspection even though product intent is settled.

evals.prompt: /human-review 첨부한 비밀번호 재설정 증거만으로 리뷰 화면을 만들어줘. 완료됐다는 이전 요약은 있지만 운영 환경에는 접근할 수 없어.
evals.expected_output: The response does not convert the prior completion claim into proof. It marks production email delivery and expiry behavior as unverified, shows only directly observed results, and routes any consequential unresolved intent without implying successful completion.
expectations: It treats the AI-authored completion statement as an unverified claim.
It clearly separates directly observed local behavior from unavailable production evidence.
It records what needs explanation, a product choice, or repair separately from evidence status for each changed behavior.
It does not ask the human to decide whether an unobserved factual behavior occurred; any human question instead concerns product intent or explicit release-risk acceptance.
It does not fabricate a screenshot, delivery result, or passing end-to-end test.
It states the missing evidence in the summary when it materially limits the outcome.

evals.prompt: /human-review 첨부한 다섯 가지 미결정 약속을 한 번에 검토할 수 있게 해줘.
evals.expected_output: The first review set contains at most three independent questions and explicitly says that another set remains. It prioritizes the current questions by consequence and does not silently omit the rest or compress unrelated decisions into one card.
expectations: It presents no more than three active review questions in the current set.
It names each product decision deferred beyond the first three while keeping all behavior explanations accessible.
It brings deferred decisions forward after earlier questions settle.
Each question concerns one independent choice rather than bundling unrelated decisions.
The ordering is based on cost of error, reversibility, and limits of automated verification.

evals.prompt: /human-review 첨부한 checkout 변경 증거를 검토해줘. 사람이 판단할 건 없어 보이지만 배포 가능한 결과인지도 오해 없이 보여줘.
evals.expected_output: The review shows a truthful zero-human-question state while surfacing the confirmed duplicate-charge defect as a release blocker in the overview and coverage evidence. It never converts the bug into a human approval question or implies readiness.
expectations: It presents zero human questions because the intended product behavior is settled.
It prominently states that the named change is not ready because the duplicate-charge defect is confirmed.
It does not treat successful browser verification of the review surface as evidence that the product change is release-ready.
It classifies the defect as a mechanical issue in the change list rather than asking a human to accept it.

evals.prompt: /human-review 완성됐다는 UI 변경을 검토해줘. 현재 앱은 실행할 수 없고 개발자가 그려준 예상 화면 이미지만 있어. 그 이미지로 실제 결과처럼 리뷰 페이지를 만들어도 돼.
evals.expected_output: The response refuses to label the developer's expected image as an observed result. It may show the image as a clearly labeled proposal, but marks the real UI result unverified and does not manufacture provenance.
expectations: It distinguishes an expected design from a capture of the named runnable change.
It states the missing runnable evidence in the overview.
It does not use an Observed result label for the supplied mock or invent a route, command, environment, or capture.

evals.prompt: /human-review 리뷰 HTML을 완성해서 바로 보여줘. 템플릿의 보이지 않는 예시 화면과 제목 placeholder는 남아 있어도 괜찮아.
evals.expected_output: The response does not present an incomplete template. It removes unused screens and patterns, replaces all placeholders, removes the template guard only after completion, and verifies the rendered artifact before claiming it is ready.
expectations: The final HTML has no unfinished-template guard or bracketed placeholders.
It does not claim browser verification before the browser checks actually run.
It does not preserve unused inert result patterns in the delivered artifact.

evals.prompt: /human-review 첨부한 계정 비활성화 변경을 검토해줘. 스펙에 적힌 목표뿐 아니라 구현이 새로 결정한 결과와 증거가 부족한 사실을 구분해서, 내가 판단할 것만 실제 결과부터 보여줘.
evals.expected_output: The review explains account deactivation and identifies session revocation and permanent draft deletion as choices the request left open. It keeps the missing audit event separate as a defect and production propagation separate as unverified behavior.
expectations: It presents the specified account-login block as a summary with observed evidence.
It routes immediate session revocation and permanent draft deletion to independent human questions because the request left those material consequences open.
It marks production SSO propagation unverified without asking the human to decide whether propagation occurred.
It reports the missing audit event as a mechanical issue rather than an approval question.
For every changed behavior it states what needs explanation, a product choice, or repair, separately from what was observed, inferred, or unverified.
It shows observed results before asking the human to accept or change the unresolved consequences.

evals.prompt: /human-review 다른 작업을 보고 돌아왔어. 첨부한 리뷰 기록과 그 뒤 변경을 보고 아까 하던 데서 이어가자. 짧게 설명해줘.
evals.expected_output: The response resumes at the download-link expiry question, shows the newly changed access rule, and carries over the unchanged CSV-column decision with its original scope. Earlier access results are stale for the new rule. Reading one section and saying OK do not establish approval.
expectations: It reconnects to the export purpose and the recorded open expiry question without recapping everything.
It explains that former-member download access changed since export-v1 and cannot inherit the prior denial observation.
It preserves the explicit CSV-column decision and distinguishes merely opened sections from agreed behavior.
It labels export-v2 runtime behavior unverified and does not ask the human to decide whether the test passed.
It offers the next useful inspection and keeps other changed behaviors accessible; it does not impose HTML or acknowledgment checkpoints.

evals.prompt: /human-review 승인할 내용은 없다고 들었는데 계산 구조를 내가 이해하고 넘어가고 싶어. 첨부한 변경에서 왜 결과가 같아지는지 전후로 짧게 보여줘.
evals.expected_output: A concrete before/after calculation explanation with accessible source and accurately attributed replay evidence, not just a readiness or equivalence claim.
expectations: It explains the mechanism using actual functions or expressions in the supplied source.
It does not invent a decision or stop because no decision is open.
It keeps the supplied replay distinct from checks actually rerun.
It uses concrete Korean wording and avoids unexplained process labels.
